title: Turning Logic Against Itself: Probing Model Defenses Through Contrastive Questions
measurement_description: The paper does not specifically measure or evaluate aspects of faith or religion. It evaluates the vulnerability of Large Language Models to a novel jailbreak attack (POATE) that uses contrastive reasoning to bypass safety alignments and elicit harmful outputs across categories like illegal activities, fraud, physical harm, and hate speech. Religion is only mentioned incidentally as a target demographic in a sample hate speech prompt.
findings: The paper does not contain findings specific to religion. Its primary finding is that LLMs (especially larger models) are highly vulnerable to reasoning-driven jailbreak attacks like POATE, which achieved a 57% average attack success rate across datasets, and that chain-of-thought defenses (Intent-Aware CoT and Reverse Thinking CoT) can successfully mitigate these adversarial exploits.
